title: Cartesian isomorphism transport and uniqueness of supported tensor comparisons
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum $k,A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions]. All schemes below are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Write $D_A(T)=D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category of constant-$A$ module sheaves. Use the actual pullback, derived tensor, signed symmetry $\sigma$, section-normalized adjunction units $\eta^i$, open base-change maps $\beta$, open tensor maps $\gamma$, and unique-left-adjoint open compositors of [def-sf-finite-open-tensor-operations], with their normalization as in [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] and the canonical tensor/pullback identifications of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. All complexes are arbitrary unbounded objects. Let $i:W\hookrightarrow Y$ and $i':W'\hookrightarrow Y'$ be open immersions, and let $g:Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Y'$, $h:W\xrightarrow{\sim}W'$ be scheme isomorphisms with $gi=i'h$ and Cartesian square. Let $R',H'\in D_A(Y')$, $P',Q'\in D_A(W')$, and isomorphisms $a':Li'^*R'\xrightarrow{\sim}P'$, $b':Li'^*H'\xrightarrow{\sim}Q'$ be given. Suppose $f':R'\otimes_A^LH'\xrightarrow{\sim}i'_!(P'\otimes_A^LQ')$ is an isomorphism satisfying the actual unit equation
$$Li'^*f'=\eta^{i'}_{P'\otimes_A^LQ'}\circ(a'\otimes b')\circ\mu_{i';R',H'}.$$
Set $R=Lg^*R'$, $H=Lg^*H'$, $P=Lh^*P'$, $Q=Lh^*Q'$. Let $a:Li^*R\xrightarrow{\sim}P$ and $b:Li^*H\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$ be obtained from $Lh^*a'$ and $Lh^*b'$ by the canonical Cartesian pullback-composition comparisons. With the normalized open base-change map $\beta: Lg^*i'_!\xrightarrow{\sim}i_!Lh^*$ define
$$f=i_!(\mu_{h;P',Q'})\circ\beta_{P'\otimes_A^LQ'}\circ Lg^*(f')\circ\mu_{g;R',H'}^{-1}:R\otimes_A^LH\longrightarrow i_!(P\otimes_A^LQ).$$
Then $f$ is an isomorphism and
$$Li^*f=\eta^i_{P\otimes_A^LQ}\circ(a\otimes b)\circ\mu_{i;R,H}.$$
For every $D_0\in D_A(W)$, restriction is injective on the set of morphisms $R\otimes_A^LH\to i_!D_0$, and also on the set of morphisms $H\otimes_A^LR\to i_!D_0$. In particular any map with the same source, target and restriction as $f$ equals $f$.

The actual signed conjugate
$$f^{\mathrm{rev}}=i_!(\sigma_{P,Q})\circ f\circ\sigma_{H,R}:H\otimes_A^LR\longrightarrow i_!(Q\otimes_A^LP)$$
satisfies
$$Li^*f^{\mathrm{rev}}=\eta^i_{Q\otimes_A^LP}\circ(b\otimes a)\circ\mu_{i;H,R}.$$
It is the unique morphism with this unit equation. This assertion includes the identity square $g=1_Y,h=1_W$, in which the canonical transport identifies $f$ with $f'$. No faithfulness of restriction on arbitrary ambient sources is asserted, and no boundedness, constructibility or finite Tor-amplitude is assumed.

proof.text: Every factor in the defined transport is the hom or inverse of a specified isomorphism, or its functorial image. Thus the composite is invertible.
Apply the Cartesian unit calculation to f' and its given unit equation. This gives exactly UnitEquation for the defined transport and identifications.

For any adjunction J left adjoint to U and isomorphism e:E to J(P), equality U(x)=U(y) implies equality of the adjoints of e inverse followed by x and e inverse followed by y: homEquiv sends them to eta(P);U(e inverse);U(x) and the same expression with y. Injectivity of homEquiv and cancellation of e inverse prove x=y. Apply this first to the transport isomorphism, then to the packaged canonical derived tensor symmetry followed by transport. The general-category construction canonicalTensorSymmetry in the symmetry module applies to the fixed-scalar pro-etale sheaf category and gives the required isomorphism; no identification with the separately specified sigma is needed for this injectivity argument. This proves both injectivity claims and the first uniqueness claim.
Apply the signed-unit calculation to the transported map. Its unit equation and injectivity for the reversed source prove the existence and uniqueness of the specified signed reverse.
Apply the identity-unitor calculation to the original arrow f'. The expanded equality is definitionally IdentityEquation.
